agree.reason: It raises the March error head-on and points to the fix, but the partner who brought that error up gets no proof the fix worked and no firm commitments, so he may stay unconvinced.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief and the error is told plainly; only the line about doing more senior-level work over the last two years goes slightly beyond the stated facts.

works_the_facts.reason: The numbers appear raw: it never says the hours ran 90 over target (about 6%), and it leaves out the strongest fact, which is no wrong or missed deadlines in about 600 entries since the check went in.

right_comparison.reason: It never says what the group loses without a formal supervisor (for example, training already happening without the title) and never puts the sheet's error record before and after the check side by side.

qualification.reason: The commitments that could be checked (certification by next June, weekly check-ins) are missing, so the bullet-point promises have no dates or measures the partner could verify.

objections.reason: It meets the deadline objection directly and frames it well as a lesson for supervising, but its only answer is the process change, not the 600-entry clean record that would actually settle the concern.

fit.reason: It is a clear letter of about 330 words, under the limit, but it still has placeholders for both names and no specific request to meet before the December 15 deadline.
